Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surat adh-Dhariyat

It is Meccan, according to the consensus of all.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾. Abu al-Tufayl narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, delivered a sermon and said: "Ask me! By Allah, you will not ask me about anything that will occur until the Day of Resurrection except that I will inform you of it. Ask me about the Book of Allah. There is no verse that was revealed except that I know whether it was revealed by night or by day, on a plain or on a mountain, and for what it was revealed." Then Ibn al-Kawwa stood up and said: "What about ﴿By those that scatter, scattering, and those that bear a burden, and those that run with ease, and those that distribute by command﴾?" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Ask for understanding, and do not ask to trouble us. ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾ are the winds; ﴿those that bear a burden﴾ are the clouds; ﴿those that run with ease﴾ are the ships; ﴿those that distribute by command﴾ are the angels." Something similar is related from Ibn Abbas, and it is the view of most of the exegetes.

As for His saying ﴿adh-Dhariyat﴾, it derives from "dharat al-rih al-turab wa adharathu" (the wind scattered the dust and dispersed it) when it spreads it apart. It is also said that the adh-Dhariyat are pregnant women who bear children, but the first view is the preferred one.
And His saying: ﴿Then those that carry a load [of rain]﴾. It was said: they are the winds that carry the clouds, and the "waqr" (load) is the clouds.

And His saying: ﴿Then those that glide along with ease﴾. It is said that they are also the winds, which move smoothly and easily. It is also said that ﴿those that glide along with ease﴾ are the seven planets: the Sun, the Moon, al-Mushtari (Jupiter), 'Utarid (Mercury), al-Zuhra (Venus), Bahram (Mars), and Zuhal (Saturn). The first opinion is the preferred one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Then those who distribute by command﴾. It is said: they are also the winds. The meaning of the "distribution of the command" is that the winds distribute the rain, so that it falls upon some places and does not fall upon others. The first opinion is the preferred one. The meaning [of the verse] regarding the angels is that they are four: Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), Isra'fil (Israfil), and 'Azra'il (Azrael). Jibril is in charge of revelation and punishment; Mika'il is in charge of provision, rain and winds; Isra'fil is in charge of the Trumpet (al-Sur); and 'Azra'il is in charge of taking souls. Al-A'sha said in describing the clouds:

(As if her walking from her neighbour's house
is the walk of the cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)

"And His saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is true﴾. Mujahid said: its meaning is that the Resurrection is certainly going to happen.

And His saying: ﴿true﴾ means: possessing truthfulness (dhu sidq). Likewise they said regarding His saying: ﴿in a pleasing life﴾, meaning: possessing pleasure (dhat rida). It is also said: the promise was called 'truthful' (sadiq) because truthfulness applies to it, just as one says 'a sleeping night' (layl na'im), 'a lying report' (khabar kadhib), 'a concealed secret' (sirr katim), and the like."

And His saying: ﴿And indeed the Judgment (al-din) is surely coming to pass.﴾ Qatada said: "Indeed the recompense (al-jaza') is surely coming to pass." Labid said in verse:

(A people who repay both kinds in kind, / evil with evil and good with good.)

He means: they are repaid (yujazun).

If it is asked: what is the meaning of swearing by the winds, the ships, the clouds and the like? How can God swear by His creation? The answer is that its meaning is: "By the Lord of the scattering winds (al-dhariyat), by the Lord of those that carry (al-hamilat), and by the Lord of those that run (al-jariyat)." It is also said: His swearing by a thing indicates the greatness of that thing and the magnitude of its benefit to the servants. It is also said: the implied construction is: "I swear by the scattering winds."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 7:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿By the sky having folds﴾. ʿIkrima said: "Possessing good creation." It was also said: "Possessing composition, firm and well-made." It is also said: "Possessing paths, as in sand and water when the winds strike them, forming patterns (ḥabāʾik)." It is said that al-ḥubk (the folds) is its splendor and its evenness. It is also said: its strength and its firmness. The poet said:

(Covered with the roots of plants, which the wind woven with a sharp gust has patterned into folds.)

And Abu Kathir al-Hudhali said:

(From among those who carried him, while they were binding (the cloth), folds of the girdle, shaking without being loosened.)

And from al-Hasan al-Basri: "By the sky having folds," that is: the stars.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are in a contradictory saying﴾ means: some affirm and some deny. It is also said its meaning is that some of them say he is a sorcerer, some say he is a poet, and some say he is a madman, and upon this the oath was sworn. It was also said: ﴿Indeed, you are in a contradictory saying﴾ means: mutually conflicting, as mentioned by al-Qaffal al-Shashi. The contradiction in this is that they acknowledged the first creation and denied the second creation, and this is a contradiction, because whoever is able to bring about the first creation is even more able to bring about the second creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿Whoever is turned away from it is turned away﴾. That is, whoever is diverted from it is diverted. It was also said: it diverts from acknowledging it whoever is diverted from it by His knowledge and decree. It is said: whoever is deprived of this good has been deprived of all good, just as it is said: whoever is denied such-and-such has been denied.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that when the affair of the Prophet spread among the tribes of the Arabs, they began to send one or two men to ask about his news. The polytheists, during the days of the season (al-mawsim, the pilgrimage season), would station people along the roads, so that when the inquirer came and asked them about Muhammad, they said: "He is a madman, a liar," and they mentioned similar things. [And they] would turn back before they met him, saying: "His own people know him best."

And His saying: ﴿Killed are the conjecturers﴾ means: cursed are the liars. This is the view agreed upon among the people of tafsir (exegesis). But it is reported from some of them that the meaning of "killed" as "cursed" is not known in the language (lughah). Its meaning is that the conjecturers have committed what deserves killing, and God's curse upon them is a destruction of them, so it is their killing.

The kharis (conjecturer) is the one who speaks by guesswork (hads) and assumption (zann).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 11:

And His saying: ﴿Those who are in a flood of heedlessness, persisting﴾. Al-Suddi said: "Heedless and distracted." It is also said: "In bewilderment and blindness." And it was said: "In doubt and ignorance," as if ignorance and blindness had overwhelmed their condition (ghamr), and from this comes "al-ma' al-ghamr" (the deep, overwhelming water), when it covers whoever descends into it. It is also said: "sahun" means they keep on going astray, meaning that doubt and misguidance persist in them.
Their saying, ﴿They ask, "When is the Day of Judgment?"﴾ means: when is the Day of Recompense? They were asking about it out of obstinacy and denial.

The Qur'anic verse ﴿On the Day they will be tried over the Fire﴾ (51:13).

And His saying: ﴿a Day when they will be tormented over the Fire﴾. That is: they will be punished. Abu 'Ubayda said: they will be burned. This was mentioned by al-Qutaybi (Ibn Qutayba) and others. It is also said: "yuftanun" means they will be made to enter the Fire, and from it comes "fatantu al-dhahab" (I smelted the gold), and we have explained this before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Taste your trial﴾ means: your punishment.

And His saying: ﴿This is what you used to seek to hasten﴾. The meaning of their seeking to hasten it is that they used to say, "When is the Day of Religion (yawm al-din)? When is the Day of Reckoning? When is the Day of Resurrection?" The intended meaning of the verse is that this is said to them.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on surah 51, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs﴾. That is: orchards and rivers.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Receiving what their Lord has given them﴾ means: taking what their Lord has bestowed upon them. The meaning of "taking" (al-akhdh) is their entry into Paradise and their arrival at the reward that they were promised.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾, meaning: before they attained what they attained, they were doers of good in the world. The meaning of ihsan (excellence, doing good) here is obedience to Allah, the Exalted. Then he explained it, saying: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they used to stand in prayer for most of the night. It is related from al-Dahhak that His saying ﴿little﴾ refers to people, and its meaning is that a few people used not to sleep. It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that its meaning is: rarely did a night pass over them in which they did not pray. Al-Husayn al-Basri said: they extended the prayer until dawn, then they sought forgiveness from Allah. It is related from Anas ibn Malik regarding its meaning: they used to pray between the Isha' and the 'Atama, and this is a transmitted report with a continuous chain (musnad). It is said that it refers to the people of Quba', who used to do this. It is related from some of them that its meaning is: they did not sleep until they had prayed the late night prayer (al-'Isha' al-Akhirah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 18:

Regarding His words, ﴿And in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾, there are two opinions. The first is that it refers to seeking forgiveness itself. The second is that its meaning is prayer (ṣalāh). Standing in prayer during the night was indeed the practice of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of those who followed them. It is narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, who was a neighbour of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he said: "How remarkable is ʿUmar: by day he fasts and attends to the needs of the people, and by night he stands in prayer."

And from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would pray for most of the night. And from ʿUthmān that he would enliven the night with one rakʿah, which was his witr. And from Ibn ʿUmar that he would sleep only a little at night. And from Shaddād ibn Aws that when he turned towards his bed, he would be like a snake on a hot griddle; then he would say: "The Fire has kept me from sleep," and then he would get up and pray until morning.

The narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ is well known: that he would stand in prayer at night and fast during the day, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made some of that easier for him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 19:

His saying: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right﴾. It is said: it is the obligatory zakat (zakat, the obligatory alms). It is also said: it is what is other than zakat of rights, namely that one carries the burdened one, joins the ties of kinship, gives in a calamity, or helps the weak.

His saying: ﴿for the beggar﴾ is the one who goes around the doors. It is also said: it is everyone who asks.

His saying: ﴿and the deprived﴾ has several views. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the muharraf (the one afflicted with poverty), who is the one for whom earning and livelihood are not made easy. It is narrated from some of them: it is the one who has no share in the spoils of war (ghanimah). But this view is considered weak, because the surah is Meccan, and the spoils came after the Hijrah.

It is also said: the deprived is the one who does not ask people, and whose condition is not noticed so that he is given.

It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah: it is the one whose wealth has been struck by a calamity (al-jaihah, a destructive disaster). This is a good view, supported by the words of God Most High in Surat Nun: ﴿When they saw it, they said: Indeed we are astray. Nay, we are deprived﴾, and their property had been destroyed by a calamity. It is also said: the deprived is the dog. This was mentioned by al-Naqqash in his Tafsir, and he related it from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. It is narrated that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz was eating while a dog was present, so he ordered that food be thrown to it, and said: "I think it is the deprived."
And His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who have certainty﴾. That is: proofs and lessons.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 21:

And His saying: ﴿And within yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said its meaning is: the passage of excrement and urine. It is also said: what enters into its belly and what comes out of it. The more preferable view is to say: it refers to all the signs within the self that indicate that it has a Creator and Maker.

And His saying: ﴿And in the sky is your provision﴾, that is, the rain. It is said that with every drop is written the provision of so-and-so.

And His saying: ﴿and what you are promised﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: the reward and the punishment. And the punishment.

Al-Kalbī said: the good and the evil. The well-known view is that it is Paradise, because it is in the sky near the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā), as the Exalted said: ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾. And from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: ﴿And in the sky is your provision﴾ is the snow, and everything that descends from the sky is melted snow.

And it is related from some of them that it may mean "And in the sky is your provision", that is, the decree of your provision.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 23:

And His saying: ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth﴾ means: the promise is true, and what you have been told, that your provision is in the heaven, and what you are promised, is true. Al-Kalbi said: "Indeed it is the truth" means: what has preceded from the beginning of the surah up to this place.

And His saying: ﴿Just as it is that you speak﴾ has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Woe to a people to whom their Lord swears an oath, and then they do not believe Him." This was narrated by al-Hasan as a mursal report. The meaning of His saying ﴿Just as it is that you speak﴾ is: it is true just as your speech is true, as a speaker says to another: "It is true just as you are here," or "as true as you are speaking."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 24:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Has the story of Abraham's honored guests reached you?﴾ We have mentioned it before. Their honoring by him was his serving them himself. It has been established, through the narration of Abu Shurayh al-Khuza'i and others, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbor; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us in Mecca, Ibn Firas informed us, Abu Muhammad al-Muqri' informed us, my grandfather Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid informed us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from [Abi] Shurayh, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the hadith.

And their honoring by him is hastening the food.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace"﴾. It is also recited as "fa-qalu salaman" (فَقَالُوا سلما). The meaning of His saying ﴿salaman﴾ is: they greeted him with a greeting (سلموا سلاما, salamu salaman). The meaning of His saying "salaman" is: "from a people at peace" (عن سلم, 'an salm).

And His saying: ﴿He said, "Peace"﴾ is his reply to their greeting.

And His saying: ﴿"A people unknown"﴾ — he only said that because he disliked their appearance, and he had not seen them before.

The poet said:

(Fa-ankartani wa-ma kana alladhi nakirtu
min al-hawadith illa al-shaybu wa-al-solaa)

And it is said: ﴿"A people unknown"﴾ means: "they are fearful"; it is said, "I disliked (ankartu) so-and-so," meaning, "I feared him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 26:

And His saying: ﴿So he turned quickly to his family and brought a fattened calf﴾. In the narrative: most of Ibrahim's wealth was cattle, and he was called "Father of Guests" (Abu al-Diyfan). It is said: he would walk a mile and two miles in search of a guest, and he would not eat except together with a guest.

And His saying: ﴿Fa-raagha﴾ means: he went off secretly.

Its wording, "So he brought it to them and said, 'Will you not eat?'" (Q. 51:27), contains an ellipsis (hadhf). Its implied meaning is: "So he brought it to them, but they did not eat; he said, 'Will you not eat?'"

As for the story: when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sat with a guest, he would lower his head and begin eating without looking at the guest. He did the same with the angels, who were four: Jibril (Jibril), Mika'il (Mika'il), Rawubil (Rawubil), and another angel. Sarah said, "Raise your head, for they do not eat." So he raised his head and said, "Will you not eat?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So he felt a fear of them in himself﴾, meaning: fear of them entered his self (nafs). In the tafsir it is related that the reason for this was that when a man was visited by a guest, he would set food before him; if the guest ate, he felt secure from him, but if he did not eat, he feared his harm.

His saying: ﴿They said, "Fear not"﴾, meaning: we are the angels of God, so do not fear.

His saying: ﴿And they gave him the good news of a learned boy﴾. The exegetes have unanimously agreed that he is Isaac, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 29:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So his wife came forward crying out in astonishment⦆, meaning: with a cry (ṣayḥa), as though she wailed the way women do. It is also said: "fī ṣarratin" is a representation of the sound of her laughter. He said in another place: ﴿and she laughed﴾. It is like the creaking of a door (ṣarīr al-bāb), the gurgling of water (kharīr al-mā'), and the qahqaha (loud laughter) being other than that; so qahqaha was derived from representing the sound of the one laughing.

As for His words: ﴿and she struck her face﴾, meaning: she struck her face, as women do.

As for His words: ﴿and said, "An old woman, barren!"﴾, she only did that because she denied that she would bear a boy while she had become an old, barren woman. We have already mentioned her age, that she was ninety-nine years old.

Translation of the passage:

And His saying: ﴿They said: "Thus said your Lord. Indeed He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing."﴾ That is: All-Wise in what He arranges, All-Knowing of the affairs of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "What is your business, O messengers?"﴾ That is: What is your affair? And for what purpose were you sent?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals."﴾ That is: disbelievers. And it was said: possessors of crime (dhawu jurm).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 33–34:

And His saying: ﴿To send down upon them stones of clay, marked (musawwamah)﴾. That is, marked (mu'allamah). It is said: the marks were like seals upon the stones. It was also said: the name of every disbeliever who would be destroyed by that stone was written upon that stone. And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿musawwamah﴾ means red in white. And it is said: streaked.

And His saying: ﴿With your Lord, for the transgressors﴾. That is, the polytheists, who are those who transgressed in acts of disobedience, and every polytheist is a transgressor in disobedience. If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿stones of clay﴾, and how can stones be of clay? The answer comes in several respects. The first: it was originally clay, then it became stone by the rising of the sun upon it.

The second: it was baked from clay, just as bricks (ajurr) are baked.

The third: His saying ﴿stones of clay﴾ mentions the clay here so that it may be known that He did not intend by it hail, whereas the Arabs call hail that descends from the sky "stones."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 33–34:

And His saying: ﴿To send down upon them stones of clay, marked (musawwamah)﴾. That is, marked (mu'allamah). It is said: the marks were like seals upon the stones. It was also said: the name of every disbeliever who would be destroyed by that stone was written upon that stone. And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿musawwamah﴾ means red in white. And it is said: streaked.

And His saying: ﴿With your Lord, for the transgressors﴾. That is, the polytheists, who are those who transgressed in acts of disobedience, and every polytheist is a transgressor in disobedience. If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿stones of clay﴾, and how can stones be of clay? The answer comes in several respects. The first: it was originally clay, then it became stone by the rising of the sun upon it.

The second: it was baked from clay, just as bricks (ajurr) are baked.

The third: His saying ﴿stones of clay﴾ mentions the clay here so that it may be known that He did not intend by it hail, whereas the Arabs call hail that descends from the sky "stones."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verses 35–36:

And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We brought out those among them who were believers. But We found not there any house of Muslims other than one.﴾ In it is evidence for the one who says that Islam (islam, submission) and iman (faith) are one and the same, and we have explained this before. It is related from Qatadah that he said: "Had there been in the towns of Lut a house of Muslims other than the house of Lut, Allah the Exalted would not have destroyed them, so that the worth of faith before Allah the Exalted might be made known."

Scholars differed as to whether anyone had believed in Lut, peace be upon him. One of the two opinions is that about ten-odd souls had believed in him. The second opinion is that no one believed in him except his two daughters.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verses 35–36:

And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We brought out those among them who were believers. But We found not there any house of Muslims other than one.﴾ In it is evidence for the one who says that Islam (islam, submission) and iman (faith) are one and the same, and we have explained this before. It is related from Qatadah that he said: "Had there been in the towns of Lut a house of Muslims other than the house of Lut, Allah the Exalted would not have destroyed them, so that the worth of faith before Allah the Exalted might be made known."

Scholars differed as to whether anyone had believed in Lut, peace be upon him. One of the two opinions is that about ten-odd souls had believed in him. The second opinion is that no one believed in him except his two daughters.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 51, verse 37:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾. That is: a lesson (ʿibrah). The lesson in the towns of Lot is clear to whoever passes by them, for it is a black land (mubayyin-ah). It is also said: the meaning of the verse mentioned, regarding the towns of Lot, is what remained of the stones in them.

Regarding the narrative, from Ibn ʿAbbas: Jibril, peace be upon him, inserted his wing beneath the seventh earth and uprooted the cities of the people of Lot from their foundations, lifted them until he brought them to the lowest heaven, to the point that the people of the lowest heaven could hear the barking of dogs and the crowing of roosters from them. Then he overturned them, and Allah, the Exalted, sent down stones upon them, as we have explained. It is also said: He sent the stones upon those among them who were scattered and travelling, until He destroyed them all.

Also regarding the narrative: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, awoke sitting in his place of worship after the angels had left. They remained with Ibrahim, peace be upon him, until they took a midday rest (qaylulah), then they set off towards the cities of Lot. The distance between the village of Ibrahim and the cities of Lot was four farsakh (leagues). When Ibrahim awoke, he saw a rising smoke in the sky from the cities of Lot, and he knew that they had been punished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 38:

His saying: ﴿And in Moses [too there is a sign], when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.﴾ That is: and in the sending of Moses there is a sign and a lesson.

And His saying: ﴿with clear authority﴾ That is: with a manifest proof.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 39:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But he turned away with his pillar﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "With his host and his troops." It is reported from Qatadah: "With his strength within himself." And it is reported from some of them: "With his clan through whom he strengthens himself." The rukn (pillar, support) of a thing is that by which the thing is strengthened. From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted, relating about Lot, peace be upon him: ﴿Or he took refuge in a mighty support﴾, meaning: in a clan and people by whom I strengthen myself. Likewise here too, its meaning is: he turned away relying on his clan and people through whom he strengthens himself. It has also been said: "He turned away with his pillar," meaning: he drew aside with his side.

And His saying: ﴿And said, "A sorcerer or a madman"﴾. The scholars said: this is a contradiction, because sorcery can only be practiced by one of complete intellect, while the madman is the one who has no intellect.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So We seized him and his hosts, and We cast them into the sea﴾ — that is, (We threw them) and cast them into the sea.

And His saying: ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ — it is said: "alama al-rajul fa-huwa mulim" (the man became blameworthy), when he has done that for which he is blamed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 51, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And in ʿAd, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾. The barren wind (al-rīḥ al-ʿaqīm) is the wind in which there is absolutely no good: it is as though it does not fertilize trees, nor stir up clouds, nor bring rain. Some exegetical reports say that the barren wind is a wind confined beneath the seventh earth, from which He sent forth an amount equal to the nostril of a bull, until it destroyed ʿAd and annihilated them, and then He returned it to the place of its confinement. It has also been firmly established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I was helped by the eastern wind (al-ṣabā), and ʿAd were destroyed by the western wind (al-dabūr)."

And it is reported from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhrī that they were destroyed by the southern wind (al-janūb). It was said to Saʿīd: "The southern wind brings mercy," and he said: "Indeed God turns it however He wills."

And it is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The barren wind is the nakbāʾ."

The Exalted's saying: ﴿It leaves nothing upon which it passes but renders it like crumbled dust.﴾ Al-Suddi said: "Like dust." Mu'arrij said: "Like ash," and he gave the word in the dialect of Hadramawt. It is also said: "Like a decayed bone that has crumbled and broken apart," and from this comes the word الرمة (al-rimma, a decayed bone). It is also said: "Like a plant that has dried out and been trampled underfoot."
And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a while." That is, for three days. We have explained this before.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they defied the command of their Lord﴾, meaning: they disobeyed. It is also said: they opposed the command of their Lord.

And His saying: ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾. It is also read as "al-Sa'qa" (al-ṣa'qah), and both have the same meaning. It is said: al-ṣa'qah is the shout (al-ṣayḥah), and al-ṣā'iqah is a derived form (fā'ilah) from al-ṣa'qah.

And His saying: ﴿while they were looking on﴾, meaning: openly, in broad daylight, while they were seeing the descent of the punishment. Its meaning is that it did not happen at night while they were asleep and unaware of it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they were not able to stand up﴾, meaning: they fell down in such a way that they were unable, after it, to rise. It is also said: they were not able to repel the punishment from themselves, meaning: to take the action of repelling. A man says: "I am not able to undertake this matter," meaning: I am not able to ward this matter off from myself.

And His saying: ﴿nor were they victorious﴾, meaning: they were not able to prevent the punishment from descending upon them.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And the people of Noah before [them]; indeed they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾. That is, they were going out of obedience to God, the Exalted.

And His saying: ﴿before [them]﴾ means: before ʿĀd and Thamūd. We destroyed them just as We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 47:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with power﴾, meaning: with strength and capability.

And His statement: ﴿And indeed, We are expanding it﴾. Mujahid said: its meaning is that Our power is wide enough to create a heaven like it. It is also said: ﴿And indeed, We are expanding it﴾ means: within Our capacity is the creation of what is more perfect and higher than this heaven that you see. The real meaning is: this which We created is not the full extent of Our power, for within Our capacity is to create the likes of this and multiples of it. It is also said: ﴿And indeed, We are expanding it﴾ means: in the provision of the servants. It is also said: in the management of the affairs of the servants.

﴿And the earth—We spread it out﴾, that is, We spread it out.

In the Tafsir of al-Naqqash (tafsir, or Qur'anic commentary): it is a distance of five hundred years.

And His saying: ﴿how excellent are the spreaders﴾, that is, the ones who spread out. The meaning is: We spread the earth in the form upon which the servants settle, and it does not tip them over, like what a person spreads as bedding to prepare a place of settling and rest for another.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 49:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And of everything We have created pairs﴾, meaning: two kinds. It is also said: the meaning is "pairs upon pairs," such as: heaven and earth, night and day, light and darkness, male and female, land and sea. It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: disbelief and faith, wretchedness and happiness, guidance and misguidance. It is narrated from al-Kalbi that he said: heaven and earth are a pair, night and day are a pair, the sun and the moon are a pair, and he enumerated a number of such things, then said: "And Allah is the Single (al-Witr)." Huthayfah narrated from the Prophet that he said: "Indeed Allah is the Creator of everything, the Maker and the thing made."

Also in some reports from the Prophet, relating from Allah, the Exalted: "There is no god but Me. I created evil, and I created the one through whose hand evil flows. So woe to the one whom I created for evil and whose hand I caused evil to flow through. And I created good, and I created the one through whose hand good flows. So blessed (tuba) is the one whom I created for good and whose hand I caused good to flow through." Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir, through the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas from the Prophet, that he said: "Indeed Allah created faith and surrounded it with generosity and modesty, and created disbelief and surrounded it with stinginess and harshness."

Also in some reports: that Allah created gentleness (rifq), so if you saw it you would see something beautiful, and He created harshness (kharq), so if you saw it you would see something ugly.

His saying: ﴿So that you may remember﴾, meaning: that you may take heed.

Almighty God's words: ﴿So flee to God﴾, meaning: from His disobedience to His obedience. It is also said: from His wrath to His mercy, and from His punishment to His pardon.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him﴾ — we have already explained this earlier.
God's saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not make with Allah another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ – the verse. We have already explained it.

Almost every word of this is about how to render the Qur'anic quotation and the explanation. The Qur'anic verse: ﴿Thus it was that no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman."﴾

The commentary: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Thus it was that no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman."﴾ Its meaning is apparent. This is a consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), i.e., just as it was said to you, so it was said to those messengers before you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an, Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 51, verse 53:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did they enjoin it upon one another?﴾ meaning: some of them instructed others with this statement. And it is said: the first of them enjoined the last of them to deny.

His saying: ﴿Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ meaning: disobedient, exaggerating in disobedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed.﴾ It is related in some reports from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that when this verse was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were greatly grieved, and they thought that revelation would no longer descend after this, since the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to turn away and withdraw, and He excused him with His saying: ﴿for you are not to be blamed.﴾

Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾, so they rejoiced. It was also said: this verse came before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 56:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, it is: "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that those among the believers should worship Me," and this is an explanation of the well-known reading.

Al-Dahhak said: The verse is general in wording, but what is meant by it is specific, namely the believers. This view was chosen by al-Farra' (al-Farra', a grammarian and Qur'an scholar) and al-Qutaybi and others.

The second view: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾, meaning: that I may command them to worship. Mujahid said: that I may command them and forbid them. Some of them reported this from Ali.

The third view: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾, meaning: that they may submit and humble themselves before Me. Their submission and humbling is their persistence in His will and His decree, and this is the meaning of the submission and obedience and compliance of the heavens and the earths. The preferred view is the first view.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 57:

The words of the Most High: ﴿I do not want any provision from them﴾ mean: that they should provide for My servants. And it is said: that they should provide for themselves.

﴿Nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ is according to the two meanings mentioned first, that is: that they should feed My servants, or that they should feed themselves. So if you say in the first case that it means providing for themselves, then the meaning is feeding the servants; and if you say in the first case that it means providing for the servants, then the meaning is that they feed themselves. He said, ﴿feed﴾ only because creation are the servants of God, so when they feed them, it is as though they fed God, by way of metaphor (majaz).

It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said, relating from God the Most High concerning what He will say to His servant on the Day of Resurrection: "I asked you for food and you did not feed Me. He will say: O Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of the worlds? He will say: My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him, and had you fed him, you would have found it with Me... the report to its end."

Almighty God says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ Al-Razzaq means al-Raziq (the Provider), and it is said that it implies intensification and abundance.

And His words ﴿Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ mean: the far-reaching strength.

God's words, "Indeed, for those who have done wrong is a portion (dhunub) like the portion of their companions," mean: a share of the punishment like the share of their companions, that is, their likes among the polytheists who came before them. He called them "their companions" because they were united in disbelief, even though the generations separated them.

Dhunub (ذنوب) in the lexicon is the large bucket, and from it the word for "share" (nasib) is derived.

God's words, "So let them not seek to hasten [it]," mean: the punishment is descending upon them, so they should not seek to hasten it, and their seeking to hasten it has already been mentioned in what preceded.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 51, verse 60:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, from their day which they are promised.﴾ We have already explained the meaning of woe (wayl). And His saying: ﴿from their day which they are promised﴾ is the Day of Resurrection, and it is the promised day awaited for the recompense of the servants. We ask Allah for a good end by His grace and His bounty, (Amin).
